title: First stopping position for word comparison
statement: For any two finite words $u$ and $v$ over a type with decidable equality, there is an index $d\le \min(|u|,|v|)$ such that every index $r<d$ contains the same symbol in both words, while at index $d$ there is no symbol present in both. Moreover, the symbols-or-absence at index $d$ are equal if and only if $u=v$.
hypotheses_covered: A symbol type with decidable equality
